title: Care & Family Legal Secretary - Huddersfield
description:
Family & Care Legal Secretary - Huddersfield Location: Huddersfield, West Yorkshire
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Job Type: Full Time Permanent
Working Pattern: Hybrid Working Available After Probation

An excellent opportunity has arisen for an experienced Family & Care Legal Secretary to join the busy Childcare and Family Law department of a well-established and highly regarded law firm in Huddersfield.

This is a fantastic opportunity for a Legal Secretary with experience in Childcare Law, Care Proceedings or Family Law who is looking to join a friendly, supportive and forward-thinking legal practice.

Working closely with experienced Care Solicitors and fee earners, you'll provide essential secretarial and administrative support on a varied caseload involving public law children matters, care proceedings and legal aid work.

The firm offers a welcoming working environment, excellent benefits, genuine opportunities for professional development and hybrid working following a successful probationary period.

The Role As a Family & Care Legal Secretary, your responsibilities will include:
- Providing comprehensive secretarial and administrative support to Care Solicitors and Family Law fee earners.
- Preparing, typing and formatting legal correspondence, court documents, statements and file notes.
- Using BigHand digital dictation to produce accurate legal documentation.
- Preparing and submitting Legal Aid applications.
- Preparing court bundles and supporting documentation for Care Proceedings.
- Opening new client files and maintaining accurate records on the case management system.
- Managing diaries, appointments and meetings with clients, counsel and other professionals.
- Liaising with clients, courts, barristers, experts and external agencies.
- Handling incoming telephone calls, emails and correspondence professionally and sensitively.
- Maintaining accurate time recording and assisting with billing administration.
- Updating experts' registers and supporting the wider Care team.
- Providing additional secretarial support and holiday cover when required.

About You Applications are welcomed from candidates who have previous experience working as a Legal Secretary within a Family Law or Childcare department, particularly those familiar with publicly funded legal work.

Ideally, you will have:
- Previous experience as a Legal Secretary, preferably within Family Law, Childcare Law or Care Proceedings.
- Knowledge of Legal Aid procedures and applications.
- Strong audio typing skills and experience using digital dictation software such as BigHand.
- Experience preparing legal documents and court bundles.
- Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing deadlines.
- A professional, compassionate and confident telephone manner.
- Strong attention to detail and a proactive approach to supporting fee earners.
- The ability to handle confidential and sensitive information appropriately.

Candidates with transferable legal secretarial experience from other practice areas will also be considered where they can demonstrate the relevant skills and a genuine interest in Family and Childcare Law.

Salary & Benefits The successful candidate will receive a competitive salary dependent on experience, together with an attractive benefits package including:
- Hybrid working available following probation.
- 25 days' annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Additional annual leave for long service.
- An extra day's holiday for your birthday.
- Two half-day Life Admin Days.
- Health scheme.
- Company pension.
- Christmas parties and team social events.
- Supportive working environment with a strong emphasis on work-life balance.

Apply Today If you're an experienced Family Legal Secretary, Care Legal Secretary or Childcare Legal Secretary looking for a new opportunity in Huddersfield, we'd love to hear from you.

This is an excellent chance to join a respected law firm where your experience will be valued and you'll play an important role in supporting vulnerable children and families.

Apply today or contact Jill McCartney at QED Legal for a confidential discussion.

title: Commercial Account Executive
description:
COMMERCIAL ACCOUNT EXECUTIVE
HUDDERSFIELD HYBRID OPTIONS
£40,000 TO £60,000, NEGOTIABLE DEPENDING ON EXPERIENCE

THE OPPORTUNITY:
Want the freedom to look after clients and grow your business in a way that works for you?
Get Recruited is partnering with a growing independent brokerage in Huddersfield to recruit a Commercial Account Executive. With referrals increasing and introducer arrangements in place for 2027, the business is preparing for a busy year.

There are existing clients available to inherit, with the allocation shaped around your experience, any business you may bring and your existing restrictions. A transferable book is preferred, but isn't essential, and the brokerage is happy to wait for relevant restrictions to expire.

For an Insurance Account Executive or Commercial Development Executive who enjoys meeting clients and building relationships, this offers flexibility over how you work and the support you use.

THE COMMERCIAL ACCOUNT EXECUTIVE ROLE:
As an Insurance Account Executive or Commercial Development Executive, you'll:
- Manage and develop client relationships, meeting businesses in person to understand their operations, risks and insurance requirements.
- Take on existing clients where appropriate, with the starting portfolio agreed around your circumstances rather than a fixed book allocation.
- Retain clients through attentive service, clear advice and regular contact, identifying opportunities to develop those relationships.
- Win new commercial business through your own relationships and prospecting, alongside opportunities arising from referrals and introducers.
- Negotiate with insurers to arrange appropriate cover and terms, keeping clients informed throughout the process.
- Shape your servicing approach: manage accounts from start to finish yourself or draw on the SME team for administration support.
- Organise your working week around client visits, business development and time with the Huddersfield team.

THE PERSON:
- Experience as a Commercial Account Executive, Insurance Account Executive or Commercial Development Executive, with evidence of retaining clients and winning business.
- Applications will also be considered from a strong commercial broker with new business experience who is ready for a more client-facing role.
- Comfortable meeting clients, understanding their businesses and developing lasting relationships.
- Self-motivated and able to manage your own workload, with a clear focus on retention and growth.
- Keen to work in an independent environment where the approach can adapt to the person and the client.
- A driving licence is essential for client visits.

If you're an Insurance Account Executive or Commercial Development Executive with existing restrictions, the brokerage is open to discussing how a move could work around them.

THE OFFER:
- Salary broadly £40,000 to £60,000, negotiable around your experience and what you can bring.
- Existing clients available, with the allocation agreed individually.
- A mainly office-based role, with one or two days working from home considered for the right person.
- Choice over whether to service accounts yourself or use the SME team for administration support.
- Flexibility over your approach, with high retention and new business the key priorities.
- Additional package elements open to negotiation.

TO APPLY:

Please send your CV for the Commercial Account Executive role via the advert for immediate consideration.

By sending an application or applying for a job, you consent to your personal data being processed and stored by Get Recruited (UK) Ltd in accordance with our Cookie & Privacy Policy (available in the footer on our website). Get Recruited (UK) Ltd acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and as an employment business for the supply of temporary workers. We are an equal opportunities employer and we never charge candidates a fee for our services.

title: Customer Specialist Sales Administrator B2B
description:
COMPANY DESCRIPTION, PROFILE AND SCOPE OF ROLE:

Our client is an established, world-leading manufacturing and engineered solutions business, backed by strong and sustained investment in capital, plant, and people. Operating as part of a prestigious international group, they supply specialist industrial solutions to blue-chip global clients across multiple engineering sectors.

Due to business expansion, they are seeking to appoint an interim Customer Service & Customs Specialist based at their Huddersfield facility. The role will initially run for a minimum of 12 months, with potential long-term prospects.

The successful candidate will provide critical B2 B customer support, manage the end-to-end UK import/customs declaration process, and oversee customer digital procurement portals. You will act as a pivotal operational link between UK clients, international distributor networks, and central European group headquarters.

NB: This role will initially last for twelve months, and may become permanent.

KEY DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:
- B2 B Order & Account Administration: Execute the full customer order lifecycle in SAP handling customer order entry, price verification, credit checks, order confirmations, delivery notes, invoicing, and sample requests.
- Customer Inquiry & Account Liaison: Act as a key point of contact for corporate customers, distributors, and external sales engineers; field phone and email inquiries, provide order status updates, and ensure high levels of service delivery.
- Customer Portals & Digital Interface: Administer digital customer procurement platforms (e.g., SAP Ariba) and partner portals, managing distributor onboarding, product documentation, and inspection certificates.
- Customer Issue Resolution & Billing Support: Support customer account management by resolving price discrepancies, handling invoice queries, assisting with dunning, and maintaining accurate customer master data in SAP.
- Customs & Import Compliance: Oversee UK import declarations (EU/international), HS code classification, duty calculations, and Northern Ireland TSS portal submissions to ensure seamless order delivery to UK customers.
- HMRC & Internal Stakeholder Liaison: Manage import VAT/duty deferment accounts with Finance, liaise with HMRC/brokers to resolve shipping holds, collaborate with European HQ compliance teams, and maintain 4-year audit-ready records.

QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE, SKILLS AND ATTRIBUTES:

ESSENTIAL
- Proven experience in an Order Management, Sales Administration, or Customer Support role within a commercial or office environment.
- Hands-on proficiency with ERP order management systems (e.g., SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle, Sage, or similar).
- Strong administrative aptitude, attention to detail, and confidence learning digital systems and customer portals.
- Excellent internal communication skills, team-player attitude, and a strong work ethic with a willingness to deliver results.

ADVANTAGEOUS NOT ESSENTIAL
- Experience within a manufacturing, engineering, distribution, or B2 B technical sector.
- Prior operational experience using SAP or SAP Ariba specifically.
- Basic exposure to UK customs/import administration, HS code classification, or Trader Support Services (TSS) for Northern Ireland declarations (full training provided).
- Formal qualification in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business Administration, or an equivalent discipline.

ADDITONAL
- The role will likely require occasional travel to the company s European HQ, so prospective candidates must hold a full UK passport and have no restrictions on travel to the EU.

Competative Salary Commensurate with Experience + Competitive Benefits

NB1: This is a temporary role, and will last a minimum of twelve months (it may become permanent, but no undertaking can be made to this effect).

NB2: The role is an onsite/office-based position based in Huddersfield.

NB3: The Agency acts as an introducer, and if successful you will be paid directly by the company engaging you and not by the Agency.

This is a varied and challenging position that would suit someone who is: Friendly, professional, and approachable Empathetic and understanding when dealing with patients Calm and resilient in a busy environment A confident problem solver Organised and able to prioritise tasks effectively Reliable, motivated, and committed to delivering excellent customer service A team player with a positive outlook Previous reception or customer service experience is desirable, and experience within a healthcare setting would be an advantage, although full training will be provided for the right candidate. Greeting patients and visitors in a professional, friendly and helpful manner. Answering telephone calls and responding to patient enquiries. Booking, amending and cancelling appointments. Signposting patients to the most appropriate service or healthcare professional. Processing prescription requests in line with practice procedures. Managing incoming and outgoing correspondence, including emails, letters and clinical documents. Registering new patients and maintaining accurate patient records. Scanning, coding and filing patient information using clinical computer systems. Liaising with GPs, nurses, hospitals and other healthcare providers. Supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. Maintaining patient confidentiality and complying with information governance requirements. Undertaking other administrative tasks as required by the practice. General Reception Duties A1. To work at the Reception Desk, greeting patients on arrival in a polite, welcoming manner. A2. To handle patient request for appointments and medication in a helpful, efficient way. A3. To answer the telephone promptly with a suitable greeting. A4. To deal with difficult, demanding patients on the phone in an appropriate manner and record telephone calls as appropriate when issues arise. A5. To ensure all messages are dealt with efficiently and appropriately making sure a contact telephone number is taken and then passed on to the relevant person(s) in an efficient and timely manner. A6. To ensure phone calls are transferred appropriately and efficiently to relevant members of staff ensuring that clinicians are free before doing so. A7. To ensuring requests from other parties (solicitors, other NHS agencies etc) are carried out within the confidentiality guidelines of the Data Protection Act (Information Governance Training will be given appropriately) and accurate records are kept of such communications as necessary. A8. To ensure online consultations requests are responded to and processed in a timely fashion A9. To advise patients of relevant charges for non-NHS and private services, accept payment and issue receipts for the same. A10. To inform the Practice Manager if a patient raises a concern or complaint with written details of the incident. A11. To complete patients request for repeat prescription items accurately and send through to the GP to sign. A12. To ensure that any items requested from the patient or patients carer that are not on the repeated items screen must requested from the Pharmacist Group detailing items requested and why they are requesting medication. A13. To deal with requests from the clinicians for patient contact or recall in an efficient timely manner. A14. To take requests from members of the public wishing to become patients issuing the appropriate information and application form and advising them of the new patient application process adopted here. A15. To ensure that all temporary patients and requests for immediate necessary treatment complete the required forms and are registered onto the system before their appointment. A16. To ensure that all New Baby registrations requests have the relevant forms completed and registered onto the system in a timely fashion. A17. To take responsibility that the signed prescription box is not accessible to the general public if ever the reception desk is left unmanned. A18. To ensure that any paper prescriptions are only collected by patients, authorised family members or pharmacies. A19. To take responsibility for all patient samples handed over the reception desk, ensuring that they have the patients details and that they are correct and are passed on to the appropriate nurse or entered into the colour coded plastic bags ready to be taken to the path labs at HRI. A20. To receive internal and external mail and deal with it appropriately, distributed to relevant trays or scanning onto the system and forwarded electronically. No items marked Private and Confidential should be opened by anyone but the intended recipient or their delegate ie, the Practice Manager will open this for the for GP when he is on leave. A21. All incoming post must be dealt with in an efficient and timely manner. A22. To input data as directed by GP, accurately and in a timely fashion onto the patients electronic record, relevant to shift worked. A23. To ensure relevant information is passed on as required for the next shift. These duties are performed by the receptionists as a team and therefore you should be able to take the initiative and perform these duties as and when required. B1. Depending on rota, to open up the surgery premises at the start of day, resetting alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. B2. Depending on rota, secure the surgery premises at end of day, ensuring all fires/heaters are switched off, all doors and windows are closed & locked, surgery is totally secured, internal lights off and alarm activated. B3. To ensure external mail is posted or taken to the post office in a timely fashion. B4. To partake in the performing of processing referral letters/medical reports/supporting letters. B5. To partake in photocopying relevant to office duties (Solicitors requests from patient files, X-ray forms and any other forms required as hand outs). B6. To ensure that the appropriate details are taken and noted accurately on the visit screen when a home visit is requested. A brief summary printout and blank prescription should also be attached and placed in the visit box in a timely manner. B7. To ensure reception and waiting areas are kept neat, tidy and safe. B8. To ensure that, after use, the patient notes are accurately filed in the correct filing system, ie alphabetical order Surname, First Name. B9. To ensure all paper waste which may contain confidential information, no longer needed, relating to the surgery or a patient is put in the shredding bins as a means of disposal. B10. To take responsibility/sign for any items deliver to the practice, ensuring that they are passed onto the intended recipient or placed in the intended area, i.e. fridge immediately. B11. To receive internal and external mail and deal with it appropriately, distributed to relevant trays or scanning onto the system and forwarded electronically. No items marked Private and Confidential should be opened by anyone but the intended recipient or their delegate ie, the Practice Manager will open this for the for GP when he is on leave. B12. To act as a chaperone when requested by a clinician for an examination and ensure a record is made of your presence on the patients record. B13. Review and process incoming emails and voicemails received in the generic email inbox. Miscellaneous C1. To be prepared to offer assistance as and when necessary due to staff shortages or to an increased workload. C2. To make every effort to attend practice meetings and training arranged by the practice even if this is outside the normal hours of work. Appropriate notice will be given and time in lieu awarded. C3. To ensure an active part is taken with the general duties of maintaining running a smooth office environment. C4. To be proactive in seeking to acquire new skills which will be to the benefit of the Practice and the role employed by the practice, such as any training courses, reading etc. C5. To follow any guidance given and adhere to the Practice Protocols written by the Doctor, Nurse and Practice Manager. C6. To take responsibility at all times for the health and safety of oneself, fellow employees and patients. C7. To be aware and comply with the practices Health & Safety Policies C8. To be aware of fire procedures, how to raise the alarm, fire fighting equipment and its use, the fire evacuation procedure and your responsibilities in an emergency situation to both patients and fellow staff members. C9. To be aware of the Practice First Aid procedures and ensure the accident book is appropriately completed as necessary. C10. To be aware of the constraints of confidentiality and in particular the Data Protection Act 2018 and its relevance to you both in, and outside of work. C11. To be aware of the Good Practice Guidelines for General Practice Electronic Records and the information contained relevant to your role. C12. To be aware of the contents of the Practice IT policies and Procedures File comply with their direction regarding the use of IT within the practice. C13. To be aware of the contents of the Practice HR policies and comply with their direction. C14. To always act within the best interest of the practice, patients and employees. C15. To support the GPs, Practice Nurses, Practice Manager and all fellow employees at all times. C16. To ensure that any other (appropriate) tasks are performed as requested by the Doctor or Practice Manager taking capacity and training into consideration.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Dalton Surgery is a family friendly practice offering a variety of services to our Practice Population. We are looking to recruit a Medical Receptionist to join our friendly team to assist with the smooth running of the Practice. The purpose of the role is to work as part of our medical receptionist team providing our patients with support and advice. Processing telephone requests for appointments. Signposting patients to the appropriated healthcare services Processing and distributing incoming and outgoing mail Taking messages and passing on information Filing and retrieving paperwork Processing repeat prescriptions. Computer data entry/data, processing and recording information. Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and outside agencies. Clearing and re-stocking of consulting rooms as required Data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning Provision of refreshments for staff and visitors as required Any other duties requested by the Practice Manager Offer general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice. Facilitate effective communication between patients, members of the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Duties and responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the practice administration team may include any or all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the Practice Manager, dependent on current and evolving practice workload and staffing levels: Opening up/locking up of practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with practice protocols Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointments system Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations, and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning Provision of refreshments for staff and visitors as required; loading and emptying the dishwasher and keeping the kitchen area clean and tidy Keeping the reception area, notice-boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice health & safety policy, the practice health & safety manual, and the practice infection control policy and published procedures. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way, free from hazards Actively reporting health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Keeping own work areas and general/patient areas generally clean, assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness consistent with the scope of the job holders role Undertaking periodic infection control training (minimum annually) Reporting potential risks identified Demonstrate due regard for safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner that is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, with such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the implementation of services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate

title: Medical receptionist
description: We are recruiting for a medical receptionist to join our friendly and busy team. This role provides reception and administrative support to the whole practice. Customer service experience and IT skills are essential. A knowledge of primary care and the IT system (System One) would be an advantage but not essential as training is provided. Good written and oral communication skills are also essential as well as good time management and organisational skills to prioritise your workload, along with an understand of, and commitment to, patient confidentiality. Welcoming patients to the surgery and providing a friendly and professional reception service.Answering incoming telephone calls promptly and dealing with a wide range of patient queries. Booking, cancelling and rearranging GP, nurse and other clinical appointments. Supporting patients with general enquiries and directing them to the appropriate service. Take accurate messages and relaying information to the relevant team members. Managing the reception area and assisting patients with check-in and other administrative queries. Liaising with GPs, nurses, administrative staff and other healthcare professionals. Maintaining accurate and confidential patient records. Handling sensitive and sometimes challenging conversations calmly, respectfully and professionally. Following practice procedures relating to confidentiality, safeguarding, information governance and patient care. Carrying out general administrative duties to support the smooth running of the practice. Please see receptionist job description attached to this advert in supporting documents. Full training will be provided.

title: Receptionist
description: The Receptionist will be responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and the provision of general support to the team. Duties can include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, the effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, the processing of information (electronic and hard copy) in a timely manner and in accordance with current policies, assisting patients as required and supporting the administration team with patient registration. The post-holder will act as the central point of contact for patients, be responsible for the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaise with team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The post-holder will be an integral part of the general practice team. a. Accurately detail information on patients records within the clinical system b. Maintain and monitor the practice appointment system c. Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments d. Answer incoming phone calls, transferring calls or dealing with the callers request appropriately e. Signpost/care navigate patients to the correct service f. Initiate contact with and respond to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies g. Input data into patients healthcare records as necessary h. Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient manner i. Support all clinical staff with general administrative tasks as requested j. Undertake a broad spectrum of administrative duties commensurate with the role k. Be an integral part of the general practice team l. Act as a chaperone as required m. Be aware of duties and responsibilities regarding current legislation and adhere to practice policies and procedures on safeguarding adults and safeguarding children n. Undertake all mandatory training and induction programmes o. Maintain a clean, tidy, effective working area at all times p. Attend a formal appraisal with their manager at least every 12 months. Once a performance/training objective has been set, progress will be reviewed on a regular basis so that new objectives can be agreed There may be, on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks. This will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels. The following are the core responsibilities of a Receptionist in delivering health services: Accurately detail information on patients records within the clinical system Maintain and monitor the practice appointment system Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments Answer incoming phone calls, transferring calls or dealing with the callers request appropriately Signpost patients to the correct service Initiate contact with and respond to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies Photocopy documentation as required Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as required Input data into patients healthcare records as necessary Direct requests for information, i.e., DSAR, insurance/solicitors letters and DVLA forms to the administrative team Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient manner Carry out system searches as requested Support all clinical staff with general administrative tasks as requested Undertake a broad spectrum of administrative duties commensurate with the role Be an integral part of the general practice team Act as a chaperone as required Be aware of duties and responsibilities regarding current legislation and adhere to practice policies and procedures on safeguarding adults and safeguarding children Support in the delivery of enhanced services and other service requirements Undertake all mandatory training and induction programmes Contribute to and embrace the spectrum of clinical governance Maintain a clean, tidy, effective working area at all times Attend a formal appraisal with their manager at least every 12 months. Once a performance/training objective has been set, progress will be reviewed on a regular basis so that new objectives can be agreed In addition to the primary responsibilities, the Receptionist has the following wider responsibilities: Support administrative staff, providing cover during staff absences Action incoming emails and correspondence as necessary Scan patient related documentation and attach scanned documents to patients healthcare records Participate in local initiatives to enhance service delivery and patient care Support in the management of repeat prescriptions, ensuring they are processed accurately and efficiently Support and participate in shared learning
